newsitem.title: UK: UK's large energy users call for assurances on tax.
newsitem.headline: UK's large energy users call for assurances on tax.

text.p: Britain's Energy Intensive Users Group (EIUG) called for assurances from the government on Friday that a proposed one-off windfall tax on utilities would not be paid by customers, particularly in the electricity market.

"We are asking the government for assurances that customers will not pay indirectly for the windfall tax and that they will address the pool's structure which earned these utilities excessive profits," EIUG chairman Ian Blakey said in a statement.
He added that "the generators have shown they can fix the wholesale price, which is unregulated, giving them an easy lever for recouping lost profit".
The EIUG has long lobbied for a review of the so-called "pool" electricity wholesale market because it claims the system favours suppliers over consumers.

The new Labour government which swept to power two weeks ago, has vowed to introduce a one-off "windfall" tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities, but has so far given few details of the measure.
